executive_summary: Cemindia’s ₹32,715 crore order book provides multi-year execution visibility, but the current quarter shows the cost of that growth: operating margins are not expanding and new equity/capex will dilute near-term return ratios. The ₹1,400 crore QIP turns the thesis into a capital-productivity test as much as an order-inflow story.
research_stance: Strong order visibility; wait for evidence that larger, more mechanized contracts improve per-share cash earnings after dilution.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹2,749.00 crore, +25.2% YoY and +1.0% QoQ. PAT was ₹131.00 crore, +21.3% YoY and -7.1% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹267.00 crore and OPM 10.00%, compared with 9.00% a year earlier and 10.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 4.77%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

The call reports EBITDA ₹280 crore including its disclosed adjustments/other-income convention versus local operating profit ₹267 crore, and a 10.2% call EBITDA margin versus 9.7% from local operating profit/sales. The company says the comparable call EBITDA margin was 11.1% last year, so local rounded OPM 9%→10% must not be treated as a clean like-for-like margin expansion. PAT increased year-on-year but fell sequentially; newer projects have not reached margin-recognition thresholds.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹500 crore and free cash flow ₹274 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹921 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 32.80% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

The audit identifies a further definition gap: call EBITDA of ₹280 crore versus local operating profit of ₹267 crore. The call also discusses October order wins alongside its ₹32,715 crore backlog; the precise cut-off needs confirmation before a September-end comparison.

thesis_drivers.title: Capital access supports bigger projects, with dilution

business_economics: Cemindia earns a project margin across engineering, procurement, labor/equipment and execution risk. Backlog indicates potential future work, but revenue recognition depends on mobilization, physical execution and certification; cash collection may lag reported profit. Data-centre electromechanical content is a large revenue component rather than an automatic premium-margin category.

The scale change also changes funding needs. A96-day working-capital metric and equipment mobilization can absorb a substantial part of new orders’ apparent economic benefit. Group-related projects contribute visibility but also concentrate order sourcing and counterparties.
earnings_quality: Revenue and PAT reconcile across the local row and call, while operating profit and EBITDA differ by₹13cr. Keep the two series separate before judging margin acceleration or calculating EV/EBITDA. Management’s10% average margin framework is more conservative than extrapolating the highest specialized-project margin across all backlog.

A call-date order book that includes October additions should not be combined with September debt and capital ratios without a dated bridge. Arbitration receipts also require separation from repeat project cash earnings, even when the underlying claim is valid.
capital_allocation: The₹1,400cr QIP must be assessed by deployment return, cash absorption and dilution. A larger equity base can lower ROE before revenue catches up; this is not merely an accounting issue because investors have supplied additional capital that needs to earn an acceptable return. Exact backlog cut-off remains an open item; it should not be assumed from the October order discussion alone.

Normal H2 capex and the large-TBM contingency are different cases. A major equipment programme requires contract visibility, utilization, mobilization economics, depreciation and exit value. Do not assume the whole₹1,500cr conditional amount is committed immediately, or exclude it when constructing a growth case that depends on the associated work.
valuation_logic: Use normalized project earnings and cash conversion after QIP dilution, with contract-specific capital needs. A backlog multiple is insufficient: specialized tunnels/marine projects and large procurement-heavy data-centre packages can have different margin and capital intensity.

The bull case requires execution and adequate equipment utilization; the base case assumes margin around management’s10% guide and staggered capex; the bear case includes delayed certification/collections, customer concentration and a low-return enlarged equity base. A price target needs post-issue share count and a funded return bridge.
peer_positioning: L&T is diversified across EPC, manufacturing, services and finance; NCC has different project mix and customer exposures; specialized tunneling contractors carry different equipment risks. Peer valuation should be adjusted for net cash/debt, working-capital intensity, contract risk and the share of group/customer concentration.
